knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A full bag or a blocked filter reduces suction and causes overheating, so both are checked before the vacuum is switched on.
Busy traffic areas are vacuumed with the pile and then against it to lift the pile. A single pass or diagonal passes leave dirt behind.
A hot smell means stop, switch off, unplug and check the bag and filter. Continuing or masking the smell both leave the overheating fault in place.
The pre-use check section says to check the test label, the plug, and the flex for damage, bare wires and tape.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied vacuum, the learner completes the pre-use check on the bag, filter, hose and beater bar, and records the result.
On a supplied floor section, the learner removes large debris by hand with gloves on before vacuuming.
The learner vacuums the supplied section edges first, then the middle in overlapping passes toward the exit, with the cable kept behind them.
On a supplied barrier mat, the learner checks the surface, the edges and the mat well, and reports the condition.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks (three questions, so all three must be correct to reach 80%; flagged for review). Practical sign-off is separate: the assessor signs off each practical criterion as observed.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Pre-use check record for the vacuum
Barrier mat condition record, where a mat is supplied
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses a vacuum with a damaged flex, bare wire, or expired test label
Learner continues to vacuum a hot or smoking machine
Learner handles a bag or filter without gloves
Learner runs the cable under the vacuum head
